newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan money rates end down on excess funds.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan money rates end down on excess funds.

text.p: Pakistan's overnight money rates slipped towards the close on Wednesday on surplus funds because of a limited open market operation by the State (central) Bank of Pakistan (SBP), dealers said.
They said overnight call rates opened with a mixed trend and early deals were struck between 12 to 14 percent. The rates crept up later and a few deals were made at 16 percent.

But the market suddenly came to life in the last trading hour as borrowers felt the SBP had mopped up only about 8.0 billion rupees in the open market operation at a cutoff yield of 16.50 percent, said a dealer at Standard Chartered Bank.
"As a result, the rates came down to 7.0 percent and the market closed with excess funds of about 1.5 billion rupees," he said. The rates were likely to slip further on Thursday.
